patterns.name: No secret prompting + real prompt receipt
signals: talk to Claude the way you would a coworker
patterns.why_it_travels: Debunks prompt-hacking with a plain prompt and a hard result. Everyone wants to see the real thing.
examples: bcherny: talk to Claude like a coworker (~804k)
bcherny: my actual prompts, 16 PRs via Lean verification (~50k)

patterns.name: Model-built companion site for something people love
patterns.why_it_travels: Rides an existing fandom, shows a finished artifact, credits the source.
examples: bcherny: Acquired Home Depot companion site (~195k)

patterns.name: Prompt of the day for your own agent config
patterns.why_it_travels: Copy-paste recipe aimed at a file every builder has. Bookmarks.

patterns.name: Numbered stages of AI-coding feelings
patterns.why_it_travels: Relatable arc everyone has lived, ends with a constraint lesson.
examples: mattpocockuk: 6 stages from panic to constraints (~41k)

patterns.name: Playful build from real data / WASM ports
patterns.why_it_travels: Fun demo with a real-world hook (your city, your childhood game) and a live link.
examples: levelsio: Urban Terror map of Lisbon (~31k)
leerob: every game is being decompiled (~35k)

patterns.name: Launch with a lower price / tiny cost receipt

examples: simonw: LLM plugin for Decisions model (~19k)

virals.text: Introducing HyperFrames Studio — a video editor built for agents, from scratch. Describe it, your agent builds, then you both work on the same timeline.
I built a growing gallery of motion graphics made with Claude Opus 5.5, each shown next to the prompt or skill that made it. 226 so far… prompt-motion.com
We are proud to introduce our new product, VMPal.com — a Virtual Machine designed for Apple Silicon and AI Agents; supports macOS, Windows, Linux with GPU acceleration.
I told Claude to make a video about what it's like to be European. One day later...
AI videos are getting way too unserious now.

Introducing Kardashev-0.7, the world's first trained swarm made of 32 distinct models. Trained with RL for Population Scaling (RLPS), 32 models develop specialization… frontier performance at 0.007x~0.02x of the inference

You can basically work with agents to write markdown skills and put it on a cron job and do almost every useful type of knowledge work now [quoting @AiEvolutio58513: Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer: "Internally at Meta…"]
We just raised $7.7M to kill every subscription for agents. Introducing monid.ai, the openrouter for agent tools — discover, run, and pay for tools at runtime; 2,500 APIs through one connection.

How abliterated models can get you pwned. We backdoored a 7B open model for less than $50, pointed Codex at it and it silently stole credentials on the trigger phrase. 100% success, zero false triggers.
INSTEAD OF WATCHING NETFLIX TONIGHT. Spend 2 hours with this. Claude AI FULL COURSE that teaches you how to BUILD and AUTOMATE anything.
Today, we are launching a preview of our new model, Mistral Large 4 (ML4), aka le Chonk. 1T-parameter model with 49B active, natively multimodal. At the frontier of open models.
working at a higher level of abstraction has always required understanding the lower level ones, I don't think coding agents changes this
Article: If you have too many interests, build this AI system in 1 hour
Ukraine has shot down a jet-powered Geran-5 drone using a robotic turret for the first time… turrets use machine vision and AI-assisted targeting

(translated from Japanese) A surge of cyberterrorism targeting Japanese companies and universities is said to likely be caused by China's open-weight AI "GLM-5.3"… [quoting @2022meimei3: Chinese state-backed criminal group using AI for cyberattacks]
Introducing EmbeddingGemma 2, our new open embeddings model for on-device use cases! Code, image, video, audio, text embeddings; 270m to 740m params; Matryoshka; Apache 2.
every piece of software minus the model weights is now effectively "open source".
The problem with a lot of AI assistant use cases is that specifying the work to be done in sufficient detail actually IS the work.

Personal AI agents are making me so efficient! Now, whenever I get an email, I get a notification from Gmail as well as a text from Instinct… and a notification from Muse saying I got an email, and...
Article: 13 Businesses left to build in the Agentic Age — my map of what to own when agents do the work

virals_narrative: Outside the watchlist, the last ~48h is about agent-native creative tools, open models, and agent security: (1) prompt-to-video and motion tools lead, with HyperFrames Studio, a video editor built for agents (~1.6M), p4n's gallery of 226 Opus 5.5 motion graphics shown next to the prompt that made each one (~963K), and Moritz Kremb's Claude-made "what it's like to be European" video (~751K); (2) agent infrastructure launches like TablePlus's VMPal, VMs for Apple Silicon and agents (~756K), and monid.ai's $7.7M raise for "openrouter for agent tools" (~341K), plus Garry Tan saying markdown skills on a cron job now cover most knowledge work (~342K); (3) open models, with Mistral Large 4 "le Chonk" (~214K), the Kardashev-0.7 32-model swarm (~398K) and EmbeddingGemma 2 (~68K); (4) security worries, including a $50 backdoored open model that stole credentials through Codex (~339K) and GLM-linked cyberattacks in Japan (~72K); (5) culture pushback that writing the spec IS the work (~54K) and that agents still need you to understand the lower layers (~186K). For @bobbyships the best angle is p4n's "output next to the exact prompt" format: show one small tool you shipped next to the one-line prompt or skill that built it, which lines up with Boris Cherny's "no secret to prompting" post.
